This error comes from this line:
https://github.com/helix-editor/helix/blob/88d6f652390922b389667f469b6d308db569bdaf/helix-lsp/src/transport.rs#L107

That's quite weird, https://www.jsonrpc.org/historical/json-rpc-over-http.html says that
> Regardless of whether a remote procedure call is made using HTTP GET or POST, the HTTP request message MUST specify the following headers:
> - The Content-Length MUST be specified and correct according to the guidelines and rules laid out in Section 4.4, Message Length, of the HTTP specification.
> - [...]

Maybe instead of implementing this here, use the [`json-rpc-client`](https://lib.rs/crates/jsonrpc-core-client) crate?

I've added `log::debug!("line: {}", buffer);` after this line https://github.com/helix-editor/helix/blob/88d6f652390922b389667f469b6d308db569bdaf/helix-lsp/src/transport.rs#L83

and those are recent lines before crash
```
2021-07-26T23:38:19.654 helix_lsp::transport [INFO] <- {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"$/progress","params":{"token":"rustAnalyzer/Indexing","value":{"kind":"report","message":"61
/751 (generic_array)","percentage":8}}}
2021-07-26T23:38:19.654 helix_lsp::transport [DEBUG] line: Content-Length: 151

2021-07-26T23:38:19.654 helix_lsp::transport [DEBUG] line:

2021-07-26T23:38:19.654 helix_lsp::transport [INFO] <- {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"$/progress","params":{"token":"rustAnalyzer/Indexing","value":{"kind":"report","message":"65
/751 (subtle)","percentage":8}}}
2021-07-26T23:38:19.654 helix_lsp::transport [DEBUG] line: Content-Length: 161

2021-07-26T23:38:19.654 helix_lsp::transport [DEBUG] line:

2021-07-26T23:38:19.654 helix_lsp::transport [INFO] -> {"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":null,"id":125}
2021-07-26T23:38:19.655 helix_lsp::transport [DEBUG] line: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"$/progress","params":{"token":"rustAnalyzer/Indexing","value":{"kind":"report","message"
:"66/751 (curve25519_dalek)","percentage":8}}}Content-Length: 160

2021-07-26T23:38:19.655 helix_lsp::transport [DEBUG] line:

2021-07-26T23:38:19.655 helix_lsp::transport [ERROR] err: <- Err(Other(missing content length))
```
It looks kinda like it would read more from buffer than it should, and Content-Length from next message is getting truncated.

~~I'm not sure if that's valid theory, but length of `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"$/progress","params":{"token":"rustAnalyzer/Indexing","value":{"kind":"report","message"
:"66/751 (curve25519_dalek)","percentage":8}}}`, the last message sent from server, has length of 162, but previous Content-Length reported length 161, maybe it's some additional byte which is added to every request, not sure.~~ Content-Length of previous messages also is equal to length+1
What's your rust-analyzer version? Someone had a similar issue a few weeks ago on nightly and it got resolved after an upgrade.

> Maybe instead of implementing this here, use the [`json-rpc-client`](https://lib.rs/crates/jsonrpc-core-client) crate?

None of the transports there actually fit, we'd need the HTTP one but over stdio. Importing hyper just to parse a single header is kinda wasteful.

---

issue.body:
closes #504

I have not tested it yet, if anyone else could confirm if it still crashes, that'd be really great.

I am also working on implementing unit-tests, however I'm not yet sure how I can make a structure that implements `AsyncRead` , there is a `Cursor` type, but the difference is that when it's empty it returns nothing, while types `ChildStdin`/`ChildStdout`/`ChildStderr` or `TcpStream` instead of returning nothing, they just return a waiting future for a new data to come.

body:
I think I see the issue: we're using `tokio::select!`, so what happens is that it polls both branches concurrently. We first poll the receiving branch, but we stop in read_exact, then during that time the sending branch receives a new event, so it executes that branch instead and the receiving branch is cancelled.

https://docs.rs/tokio/1.9.0/tokio/macro.select.html#cancellation-safety

> The following methods are not cancellation safe and can lead to loss of data:
>    tokio::io::AsyncReadExt::read_exact

I think this is why jsonrpc-client duplex implements it's own future: https://github.com/paritytech/jsonrpc/blob/dc6b8ede1e86feb32a2bbe4770628ee3788b3f4d/core-client/transports/src/transports/duplex.rs#L94-L101
